entry.name: juqiao glove 0929
entry.title: juqiao glove 0929
entry.authors: NIRC Computer Vision Lab and Addx Technology
entry.summary: JQ (juqiao) fabric tactile glove, 132 raw ADC taxels per hand (12 per fingertip, 72 on the palm), recorded with one static RGB camera and reconstructed MANO-based hand states over 11 pick and manipulation recordings of household objects, two of them bimanual.
entry.hand: JQ tactile glove (right hand; both hands in 2 of 11 recordings)

sensor.note: Per recorded hand: <side>_tactile_data_fingers (T, 5, 12) and <side>_tactile_data_palm (T, 1, 72), raw 8-bit ADC 0-255 stored as float32. All 12 finger taxels sit on the distal link of each finger; the palm block has 56 taxels on the palm and 16 on the thumb base link (channel_mapping.json). Each 10 Hz value is the median of the raw samples within +/-50 ms of the camera frame (raw glove rate about 81 Hz, 4,745-5,759 samples per recording); no baseline subtraction, threshold or force calibration. 132 of the glove's 256 raw channels are bound; left and right mappings differ.

scale.text: 11 recordings (45-90 s), 16 continuous spans, 7,126 frames at 10 Hz (11.9 min), 10 household objects; 8 single-object picks, 1 single-hand manipulation, 2 bimanual

entry.access: Hugging Face lilfiiiiish/juqiao-glove-0929, ungated, 3.3 GB of Zarr v2 directories (one per recording, one blosc-compressed RGB chunk per frame).
caveats: Very small: 11 recordings from one day (2026-09-29), one external camera, 10 objects; 9 of 11 recordings have the right hand only, and an absent hand has no arrays (no zero filling).

Tactile values are raw ADC with standing readings: in the first 5 frames of every recording most regions already sum to 6-140 ADC, and the pinky and palm regions are almost never 0, so contact has to be judged against a baseline. The README warns of glove and posture noise and says a low ADC does not certify no contact.

Hand state is a 21-D vector of FTP-1 geometric angle features in radians plus a 6-D wrist pose (metres, rotation vector) in the camera frame, reconstructed by an unnamed method; the README says it is not motion-capture ground truth. Depth, extra RGB views and IMU from the capture were not released.
Instructions were drafted from file names ('Pick up the cola can.') and are flagged as needing review; the 16 spans are data-continuity breaks, and 4 recordings start with a 1-frame span.
Published 2026-10-16 as an Open-X-Tactile (OXT) contribution; OXT acceptance is not claimed. pinkcup_pick_0929 was excluded (missing visual timestamps).

unconfirmed: Glove maker: the card names the sensor 'juqiao glove'; 'juqiao' is the pinyin of 矩侨 (JQ Industries), maker of the catalog's jq_tactile_glove (256 raw channels in EgoTouch). The raw CSVs here have columns p1-p256, of which 132 are bound.
episodes=16 are the continuous spans (meta/episode_ends); the card says no action labels or split exist. tasks=11 is the metadata.json 'task' count (one draft instruction per recording).
objects=10 counted from recording names (black cup, cola can, coffee bottle, coffee box, cookie box, green spray bottle, pink spray bottle, Lay's snack can, soup can, capybara toy).
Raw glove rate about 81 Hz derived from export_report.json raw_adc_samples / recording duration (80.8-81.3 Hz in all 11).
scenes=1 and scene_type 'lab' from one RGB frame (optical breadboard table, robot arms at the edges). Subjects not stated; source paths contain 'subject_fbs', which suggests one subject.
Institutions: the card names 'NIRC Computer Vision Lab' and 'Addx Technology' with a bupt.edu.cn contact address; their Chinese names were not found.

sample.fetch_estimate: ~1.4 GB (RGB chunks of the 7 windows at ~460 KB per frame, ~2,900 frames; tactile and pose arrays < 10 MB)
sample.rules_applied: 11 recordings, each its own instruction (more than 6), so 7 are taken: both bimanual recordings, the single-hand manipulation recording, and 4 picks spanning a box, a soft toy, a snack can and a soup can. One episode per task. Recordings longer than 60 s are cut to a 40 s window chosen by the largest tactile energy (sum over taxels of value minus that taxel's 10th percentile); the window still has to be checked against the video for contact in step 3, because the raw ADC has standing readings from the first frame.
deviations: Contact was judged from region sums above 30 ADC; with no baseline in the data, the step-3 converter should subtract a per-taxel rest level before calling a frame 'contact'.
